chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: Chicken in the basket song and Vine Street Varieties
summary: Ramey's jingle on 'Pennies from Heaven', the Saturday show at the Lincoln Theater and Dave Dexter's fondness for McShann.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: He took care of business very good at the Martins, and in fact they loved him out there. We made a tune -- they had a special food that they were promoting, chicken in the basket. And I made up a song on it, on "Pennies from Heaven," you know. I put some other words to it.
But you changed the melody a bit?
No, just used the melody and just used it just for that house there.

And we'd sing it there, and sometimes we'd do it on the radio. Nobody ever bothered it. But it was chicken in the basket, and how it would knock you out. So people were coming from all over. I mean, the right society of people, because they wouldn't let a bum in there, you know. They -- everybody would come in and you'd see them order chicken in the basket. Turned out to And that would be a great thing. McShann And during that time Max Hammond (PHONETIC) was so popular we got that thing called the Vine Street Varieties. This was Saturday night, at the Lincoln (PHONETIC) Theater there, we would do a show for the black people. And it would start at about 12:30 and go until about 4:00 or 3:30, you know.

one show. But we'd go on with McShann's group. They had a comedian, couple of singers around. And maybe a shake at that place. dance or something, you know. On the stage there. And McShann's popularity just grew. People down at the radio station, everybody was trying to get McShann. Then Dave Dexter met him and he fell in love with him. From there on, McShann was making it.
Well, what you're saying there is this is part -- as much personality as his music, isn't it?
